svg.text: WHY BUFFERS SIT 256 MB APART. An in-place FFT stalls on silicon: the DMA is
still flushing transform t while the feeder pulls t+1 over the shared
interconnect, CoreFFT drops BUF_READY and the pipeline locks. Ping-ponging
SCRATCH <-> SIG keeps read and write on SEPARATE 256 MB pages.
An 8192 x 8192 complex frame is 256 MB, so no stage fits on chip and every stage streams through FIC_0. The design
is therefore BANDWIDTH-bound, not compute-bound -- MACC utilisation is 74 of 784 (9%). Deleting a DDR pass is worth
